requirement_text.REQ-063: Execute Decision 0006's D1 (docs/migration/decisions/0006-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md): relocate REQ-015's users, groups and tenant_role tables out of the public default schema and into each tenant's own Postgres schema, via the same :prefix mechanism and the same TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0 registry every business table already uses. See handoffs/WF02-REQ063-20260818/step-01-code-designer.json for the full text (unchanged, not re-copied here to keep this handoff shorter -- read it there).

task.description:
RE-GATE after rework iteration 1. CODE-DESIGNER added a new §5b to lib/letflow/design/req063-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md addressing the single BLOCKER from your prior FAIL (check 2a, the identity.ex prefix-threading TBD). Read §5b directly and confirm it is now concrete, not illustrative: a real @spec for provision_oidc_user/4 (arity changed from /3) with an opts :: [prefix: String.t()] parameter matching lib/letflow/definitions.ex's actual established convention (confirm CODE-DESIGNER actually grepped/read definitions.ex rather than citing it from memory -- check the cited line number and pattern shape match what's really in that file), the same threading through upsert_by_external_identity/4, insert_or_fetch/4, re_select_on_conflict/3, get_by_external_identity/3, the exact AuthPipeline.provision_user/3 call-site edit (deriving the prefix via TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 on the already-resolved tenant_id), and a stated error-shape consequence (or explicit confirmation of none). Confirm resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 and verify_realm_ownership/2 were correctly left unchanged (they only touch the public-schema Tenant table) -- the fix should not have expanded beyond provision_oidc_user's own chain. If §5b still just gestures at a shape without full signatures for every function in the chain, that is still a check-2a FAIL, rework iteration 2.

Also re-verify the five originally-passing checks were NOT accidentally broken by this rework (spot check, not a full re-read is fine for these five, since they were untouched by the rework instruction): three migrations' prefix() guards, the divergence-closure header comment, tenant_role's join-through-groups partitioning, the drop migration's separation, and the tenant_id-not-dropped scope statement.

Original Step 1b instructions below, still applicable for anything not superseded by the RE-GATE paragraph above: Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req063-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md against REQ-063's acceptance criteria and decision 0006. Read the design artefact directly -- do not read CODE-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute.

Pay particular attention to a gap CODE-DESIGNER's own summary flagged as newly surfaced (not named in decision 0006 or the requirement text): Letflow.Identity's existing functions (provision_oidc_user/3, resolve_tenant_by_realm/1, etc.) have no :prefix threading today, and will break the moment the public users/groups/tenant_role tables are dropped by this design's step-4 drop migration. Confirm the design actually addresses this as a hard precondition (not silently assumed away) -- if the design defers it to REQ-063's own implementation step without a concrete plan, that's a design gap significant enough to fail on: ELIXIR-DEV needs to know at implementation time whether Letflow.Identity's public functions need a prefix/tenant_schema parameter added, and if so, what every existing caller (notably lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex) needs to change to. A design that says 'this needs fixing' without saying how is a TBD deferral and fails check 2a below.

Also specifically verify: (1) all three migrations carry REQ-022 section 4's prefix()-truthiness guard: (2) the users migration's index shape correctly closes the (tenant_id, external_realm, external_id) vs (external_realm, external_id) divergence decision 0006 section 3.2 names, with the header-comment requirement stated; (3) the data-copy mechanism's function signature handles tenant_role correctly -- it has no tenant_id column, so per-tenant partitioning must go through a join via groups, confirm the design actually specifies this rather than assuming tenant_role has a tenant_id column it doesn't have; (4) the drop migration is a genuinely separate migration from the three create migrations, not bundled; (5) the design explicitly and clearly states tenant_id is NOT dropped by this design (that's REQ-064).
acceptance_criteria: Every MUST/acceptance criterion has a corresponding design element, no TBD/deferral language
The newly-surfaced Letflow.Identity :prefix-threading gap is addressed concretely, not deferred without a plan
Function signatures fully specified (name, inputs, outputs, error cases)
Error handling shape stated ({:ok,_}|{:error,_} tags, not left implicit)
No implementation code present (no .ex/.exs code bodies -- signatures and type shapes only)
tenant_role's lack of a tenant_id column is correctly handled in the data-copy design, not assumed away

issues.check: REQ-022 §4 prefix()-truthiness guard on all three create migrations
issues.finding: Independently confirmed present and correctly specified for all three (groups, tenant_role, users) -- no issue, non-blocking.

issues.check: users migration index-shape divergence closure (tenant_id,external_realm,external_id) vs (external_realm,external_id)
issues.finding: Independently confirmed correctly closed and explicitly stated as a header-comment requirement, matching decision 0006 §3.2's framing exactly (relocates rather than removes the global guarantee, via tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index). No issue, non-blocking.

issues.check: tenant_role has no tenant_id column -- data-copy must partition via join through groups
issues.finding: Independently confirmed the design does NOT wrongly assume tenant_role has a tenant_id column -- it explicitly states 'tenant_role requires special handling: it carries no tenant_id column' and specifies the join-through-groups query shape plus an orphan-row error case ({:error, {:orphaned_tenant_role, tenant_role_id}}). No issue, non-blocking.

issues.check: drop migration is a genuinely separate migration, not bundled
issues.finding: Independently confirmed as a separate file/module (DropLegacyPublicIdentityTables) from §2's three create migrations, explicitly stated as never-bundled, matching GBL-112 precedent. No issue, non-blocking (though see the BLOCKER above -- being structurally separate does not resolve the identity.ex precondition gap for when it is safe to run).

issues.check: design explicitly states tenant_id is NOT dropped by this design (reserved for REQ-064)
issues.finding: Independently confirmed stated explicitly and repeatedly (top-level scope boundary plus both per-migration header-comment requirements). No issue, non-blocking.

Confirmed no defmodule/def blocks anywhere in the file (grep returned zero matches). Inline Repo.all(from(...))/Repo.insert(...) fragments at lines 70, 346, 348, 353, 364 are prose-level query-shape specification (illustrating what a query selects/inserts), not code bodies with control flow -- consistent with specification altitude elsewhere in this design (e.g. req043's prior designs use the same convention). Does not itself fail check 2e. No issue, non-blocking.
